transcript.text:
This can be caused by a few things, ranging from a normal programme feature to an electrical fault. The most common cause is that the dryer has entered an 'Anti-crease' or 'Refresh' mode at the end of a cycle. This is normal behaviour. If it's not doing that, it could be a stuck start button on the control panel, or less commonly, a fault with the main control board (PCB) keeping power to the motor. 1. When you say it 'won't stop', does the drum actually keep turning for a long time after the cycle should have finished? Or is it just making noise/trying to run but not tumbling?
2.
it shows End but the drum keeps turning for a bit every couple of minutes. stops if i open the door

From what you have described, the most likely cause is door/interlock wiring. Check the dryer's plug is pushed fully in and the socket is on, and try another appliance in that socket. If the house electrics have tripped, don't keep resetting it. Was a switch, plug or fuse off (and is it sorted), or does the socket work fine with something else?
the plug is in and nothing has tripped. it dries the clothes fine, it only turns after it says End

This sounds like the 'Anti-crease' or 'Refresh' feature, which is normal behaviour on many dryers to tumble clothes gently every few minutes after drying so they don't crease. However, if it keeps running indefinitely or doesn't stop when you expect, the control board may be stuck in this mode. Please try a full reset: unplug the dryer (or switch off the circuit breaker) for 1 minute to clear any electronic glitches. Plug it back in and run a short drying cycle. Watch what happens at the end. If it stops turning after 'End', it was just a glitchy anti-crease mode. If it continues running even after the reset, the control board is likely faulty.
ok i will try that. what is anti-crease? it keeps going for about an hour if i leave the clothes in

Anti-crease (sometimes called Refresh) is a feature designed to stop your clothes from creasing while they sit in the drum after drying. Instead of stopping completely and letting the damp heat settle into folds, the dryer gently tumbles the clothes every few minutes for up to an hour or so. Based on what you've told me—that it shows 'End', dries the clothes fine, but then turns intermittently for about an hour before stopping when you open the door—this is probably normal operation. It is not a fault. If you prefer your clothes to stop tumbling immediately once dry, check your dryer's manual (or look for a button with a 'Refresh' or anti-crease symbol) to see if you can turn this feature off before starting the cycle. If it continues running indefinitely long after that hour mark, or starts heating up again at the end, then we would need to look at the control board.
